entries.note: DOI resolves to Akama 2009 (PMID 19303290); quote verbatim in abstract. PBMC LPS/PHA/ConA cytokine assays confirmed in FDA PharmR. Opening untested is correct.
Bissonnette 2019 (PMID 31419544, epub 2019-08-13; NCT03233529 results 2019-08-13). Quote verbatim. Pairing of PBMC cytokine release with lesional Th2/Th17 transcripts; downstream tier is right.
Quote verbatim in PharmR. 3-month minipig study was reviewed under the IND before the 6-month rat study (initiated 2012-06-19), so a 2011 proxy is plausible.

Quote verbatim; minipig AUCs 1,080-1,450 ng·h/mL. NOAEL 5% (above 2% clinical strength) existed pre-Phase 3; the AUC margin itself is stated only in the 2016 review, after the trials. See rule question.
Quote verbatim in Akama abstract; PharmR names mouse phorbol ester ear edema with 74% inhibition by clinical formulation, the only in vivo efficacy model in the review.

Paller 2016 (PMID 27417017, epub 2016-07-11) quote verbatim; label table matches 32.8/25.4/31.4/18.0. Primary endpoint. LEO 29102 indeed went in on mouse allergic contact dermatitis, difamilast on mouse chronic contact dermatitis, so neither lands on this model.
Rabbit irritation and negative LLNA quotes verbatim in PharmR. 2010 proxy reasonable.
Label line 436 verbatim (patient information). Application-site pain is the common adverse reaction; partial is fair since rabbits graded erythema/edema.

missing: LEO 29102 (member): Phase 2 NCT01037881 primary endpoint (EASI change) not significant vs vehicle for any dose (p=0.27, 0.83, 0.08, 0.16), results posted 2019-10-14. Model = mouse topical allergic contact dermatitis (Felding 2014, doi:10.1021/jm500378a, which called the efficacy 'clinically relevant'). This is a contra for a second model_id (mouse-acd) dated 2019, currently buried in patient_trials with no status. It does not lower the crisaborole model's cell under the best-model rule, but it should be recorded.

DRM02 (member): Dermira 10-K filed March 2015 (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1557883/000104746915002713/a2223853z10-k.htm): 'Initial efficacy data in proof-of-concept clinical trials indicated that DRM02 gel was not more effective than vehicle-only gel'. Tier 5 failure (NCT01993420, no posted results). Its model side was not found, so it scores untested or is set aside, but the note should say it failed rather than 'stopped'.

Difamilast (member): its FDA multidiscipline review (NDA 219474) names a mouse chronic contact dermatitis model; the Japanese Phase 2/3 primary IGA endpoints were met. A same entry for a separate model_id; the cell status does not change.
rule_questions: When several class members went in on different efficacy models (crisaborole: TPA ear edema; LEO 29102: mouse allergic contact dermatitis, failed primary; difamilast: chronic contact dermatitis), must the cell record every model's track as its own entries, or only the best model's? The rule 'one drug's contra beats another drug's same on the same model' does not say what happens across models within one cell.

Decision 16 margin_stated: the minipig NOAEL (5% ointment, above the 2% clinical strength) was filed under the IND before Phase 3, but the AUC-based margin (about 1x) was first stated in the 2016 NDA review using patient PK. Does a pre-trial NOAEL at a higher strength count as a stated margin, or does the margin need to be expressed in exposure before the trial?

Does a sponsor's own optimistic reading in a tier-1 paper (Felding 2014: 'clinically relevant efficacy') hold the status until the registry posts a failed primary (2019), per rule 7 (what was known at the date)?
